newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soy losses from frost may be 35 mln bu - Brock.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soy losses from frost may be 35 mln bu - Brock.

text.p: A frost last weekend in parts of Iowa, Minnesota and North Dakota may have destroyed as much as 35 million bushels of soybeans, said Jeff Wilson, editor of the Brock Report.

"It appears that it was a little bit more widespread than the trade believed yesterday," Wilson said. "Yesterday (agronomists) were saying (frost damage) six inches down. Now they're saying 12 inches and they're afraid it goes deeper than that."
He estimated losses at between 15 million and 35 million bushels but added "I'm leaning toward the lower end of that."
Temperatures as low as 29 degrees Farenheit were reported Saturday morning in Minnesota. The cold weather may also have hurt corn but Wilson said it was too early to assess damage.
"It's going to take another couple of days," Wilson said. "It's very difficult to put a number on the crop loss until we see how the rest of the (U.S.) crop looks."
